title: Alias order
prompt: Show each title and price * 1.2 as with_tax, keeping only rows where that calculation is above 20. Repeat the calculation in WHERE. Replace the ___.

cases.name: Different data
cases.setupSql: DELETE FROM books; INSERT INTO books VALUES (10, 'Copper Moon', 'Ada Hill', 'Fantasy', 20.0, 100, 2020), (11, 'North Light', 'Raj Dev', 'Travel', 7.5, 180, 2015), (12, 'Sky Atlas', 'Ada Hill', 'Science', 25.0, 300, 2023); UPDATE books SET price = 18.0 WHERE id = 10;

solutions: SELECT title, price * 1.2 AS with_tax FROM books WHERE price * 1.2 > 20;

wrongSolutions.sql: SELECT title, price * 1.2 AS with_tax FROM books WHERE price > 20;
SELECT title, price * 1.2 AS with_tax FROM books;

title: Sorting by an alias
prompt: Show each title and pages * 2 as minutes, longest first. ORDER BY runs late, so use the alias there.

cases.name: Different data
cases.setupSql: DELETE FROM books; INSERT INTO books VALUES (10, 'Copper Moon', 'Ada Hill', 'Fantasy', 20.0, 100, 2020), (11, 'North Light', 'Raj Dev', 'Travel', 7.5, 180, 2015), (12, 'Sky Atlas', 'Ada Hill', 'Science', 25.0, 300, 2023);

solutions: SELECT title, pages * 2 AS minutes FROM books ORDER BY minutes DESC;

wrongSolutions.sql: SELECT title, pages * 2 AS minutes FROM books ORDER BY minutes;
SELECT title, pages * 2 AS minutes FROM books ORDER BY title DESC;

title: Rows, then groups
prompt: Count each customer's shipped orders as shipped, keeping customers with at least 1. Use WHERE for shipped and HAVING for the count.

cases.name: Different data
cases.setupSql: DELETE FROM order_items; DELETE FROM orders; DELETE FROM products; DELETE FROM customers; INSERT INTO customers VALUES (7, 'Ravi', 'Oslo', 'ravi@mail.test', '2024-05-05'), (8, 'Sara', 'Lima', NULL, '2024-06-06'), (9, 'Tom', 'Oslo', NULL, '2024-07-07'); INSERT INTO products VALUES (7, 'Stool', 'Home', 40.0, 25.0), (8, 'Cup', 'Kitchen', 9.0, 2.0), (9, 'Ink', 'Stationery', 12.5, 6.0); INSERT INTO orders VALUES (11, 7, '2024-02-28', 'shipped'), (12, 8, '2024-03-01', 'pending'), (13, 7, '2024-03-31', 'cancelled'); INSERT INTO order_items VALUES (11, 7, 1, 4.0), (11, 8, 3, NULL), (12, 9, 2, NULL), (13, 8, 1, NULL);

solutions: SELECT customer_id, COUNT(*) AS shipped FROM orders WHERE status = 'shipped' GROUP BY customer_id HAVING COUNT(*) >= 1;

wrongSolutions.sql: SELECT customer_id, COUNT(*) AS shipped FROM orders GROUP BY customer_id HAVING COUNT(*) >= 1;
SELECT customer_id, COUNT(*) AS shipped FROM orders WHERE status <> 'shipped' GROUP BY customer_id;

title: Top group
prompt: Show the department_id with the highest total salary, and that total as total. Leave out employees with no department.

cases.name: Different data
cases.setupSql: DELETE FROM employees; DELETE FROM departments; INSERT INTO departments VALUES (5, 'Design'), (6, 'Finance'), (7, 'Ops'); INSERT INTO employees VALUES (11, 'Ivy', 5, NULL, 90000, '2019-02-01', 900, 'ivy@acme.test'), (12, 'Jon', 5, 11, 70000, '2020-06-15', NULL, NULL), (13, 'Kim', 6, 11, 70000, '2023-03-03', 300, 'kim@acme.test'), (14, 'Leo', NULL, 77, 30000, '2024-08-20', NULL, 'leo@acme.test'), (15, 'Mia', 6, 13, 55000, '2022-12-31', 0, 'mia@acme.test');

solutions: SELECT department_id, SUM(salary) AS total FROM employees WHERE department_id IS NOT NULL GROUP BY department_id ORDER BY total DESC LIMIT 1;

wrongSolutions.sql: SELECT department_id, SUM(salary) AS total FROM employees GROUP BY department_id ORDER BY total LIMIT 1;
SELECT department_id, MAX(salary) AS total FROM employees WHERE department_id IS NOT NULL GROUP BY department_id ORDER BY total DESC LIMIT 1;

title: DISTINCT before LIMIT
prompt: Show the top 2 different product categories in reverse alphabetical order.
hints: DISTINCT happens before ORDER BY and LIMIT.

cases.name: Different data
cases.setupSql: DELETE FROM order_items; DELETE FROM orders; DELETE FROM products; DELETE FROM customers; INSERT INTO customers VALUES (7, 'Ravi', 'Oslo', 'ravi@mail.test', '2024-05-05'), (8, 'Sara', 'Lima', NULL, '2024-06-06'), (9, 'Tom', 'Oslo', NULL, '2024-07-07'); INSERT INTO products VALUES (7, 'Stool', 'Home', 40.0, 25.0), (8, 'Cup', 'Kitchen', 9.0, 2.0), (9, 'Ink', 'Stationery', 12.5, 6.0); INSERT INTO orders VALUES (11, 7, '2024-02-28', 'shipped'), (12, 8, '2024-03-01', 'pending'), (13, 7, '2024-03-31', 'cancelled'); INSERT INTO order_items VALUES (11, 7, 1, 4.0), (11, 8, 3, NULL), (12, 9, 2, NULL), (13, 8, 1, NULL); INSERT INTO products VALUES (10, 'Zip', 'Zoo', 1.0, 1.0);

solutions: SELECT DISTINCT category FROM products ORDER BY category DESC LIMIT 2;

wrongSolutions.sql: SELECT category FROM products ORDER BY category DESC LIMIT 2;
SELECT DISTINCT category FROM products ORDER BY category LIMIT 2;

title: Fix the order of clauses
prompt: This should show the average grade per course as average for courses averaging over 70, highest first, but the clauses are out of order. Fix it.
starterSql:
SELECT course_id, AVG(grade) AS average
FROM enrolments
ORDER BY average DESC
HAVING AVG(grade) > 70
GROUP BY course_id;
hints: The written order is SELECT, FROM, WHERE, GROUP BY, HAVING, ORDER BY.

cases.name: Different data
cases.setupSql: DELETE FROM enrolments; DELETE FROM courses; DELETE FROM students; INSERT INTO students VALUES (6, 'Femi', 9), (7, 'Gia', 9), (8, 'Hao', 10); INSERT INTO courses VALUES (5, 'Chemistry', 'Science'), (6, 'Drama', 'Arts'); INSERT INTO enrolments VALUES (11, 6, 5, 60, '2023-autumn'), (12, 6, 5, 60, '2024-spring'), (13, 7, 5, NULL, '2024-spring'), (14, 7, 6, 95, '2024-spring'); UPDATE enrolments SET grade = 50 WHERE id = 14;

solutions: SELECT course_id, AVG(grade) AS average FROM enrolments GROUP BY course_id HAVING AVG(grade) > 70 ORDER BY average DESC;

wrongSolutions.sql: SELECT course_id, AVG(grade) AS average FROM enrolments GROUP BY course_id ORDER BY average DESC;
SELECT course_id, AVG(grade) AS average FROM enrolments GROUP BY course_id HAVING AVG(grade) > 70 ORDER BY average;

title: Aggregate in ORDER BY
prompt: Show each city and its number of customers as customers. Sort by the count from highest to lowest, then by city.
hints: Sort by count, then break ties.

cases.name: Different data
cases.setupSql: DELETE FROM order_items; DELETE FROM orders; DELETE FROM products; DELETE FROM customers; INSERT INTO customers VALUES (7, 'Ravi', 'Oslo', 'ravi@mail.test', '2024-05-05'), (8, 'Sara', 'Lima', NULL, '2024-06-06'), (9, 'Tom', 'Oslo', NULL, '2024-07-07'); INSERT INTO products VALUES (7, 'Stool', 'Home', 40.0, 25.0), (8, 'Cup', 'Kitchen', 9.0, 2.0), (9, 'Ink', 'Stationery', 12.5, 6.0); INSERT INTO orders VALUES (11, 7, '2024-02-28', 'shipped'), (12, 8, '2024-03-01', 'pending'), (13, 7, '2024-03-31', 'cancelled'); INSERT INTO order_items VALUES (11, 7, 1, 4.0), (11, 8, 3, NULL), (12, 9, 2, NULL), (13, 8, 1, NULL);

solutions: SELECT city, COUNT(*) AS customers FROM customers GROUP BY city ORDER BY customers DESC, city;

wrongSolutions.sql: SELECT city, COUNT(*) AS customers FROM customers GROUP BY city ORDER BY city;
SELECT city, COUNT(*) AS customers FROM customers GROUP BY city ORDER BY customers, city;

title: All the steps
prompt: Considering sessions of at least 10 minutes, show each user_id with a total above 30 minutes as total. Sort from highest to lowest, and return the top 2.
hints: Use all of WHERE, GROUP BY, HAVING, ORDER BY, and LIMIT.

cases.name: Different data
cases.setupSql: DELETE FROM sessions; DELETE FROM users; INSERT INTO users VALUES (7, 'sable', NULL, '2024-02-27'), (8, 'tulip', 7, '2024-02-28'), (9, 'umber', 7, '2024-03-01'); INSERT INTO sessions VALUES (11, 7, '2024-02-28', 50, 'web'), (12, 7, '2024-02-29', 50, 'web'), (13, 7, '2024-03-01', 7, 'ios'), (14, 8, '2024-03-02', 33, 'android'); DELETE FROM sessions WHERE user_id = 7; INSERT INTO sessions VALUES (15, 9, '2024-03-02', 8, 'web'), (16, 9, '2024-03-03', 25, 'web');

solutions: SELECT user_id, SUM(minutes) AS total FROM sessions WHERE minutes >= 10 GROUP BY user_id HAVING SUM(minutes) > 30 ORDER BY total DESC LIMIT 2;

wrongSolutions.sql: SELECT user_id, SUM(minutes) AS total FROM sessions GROUP BY user_id HAVING SUM(minutes) > 30 ORDER BY total DESC LIMIT 2;
SELECT user_id, SUM(minutes) AS total FROM sessions WHERE minutes >= 10 GROUP BY user_id ORDER BY total DESC LIMIT 2;
